excerpts.source_text: Unrestricted amounts of cash, i.e. notes and coins, foreign currencies and bearer negotiable instruments (shares, bonds and cheques) may be carried into, through and out of Switzerland.

excerpts.source_text: Im Sinne dieser Verordnung bedeuten: a. auskunftspflichtige Person: anmeldepflichtige Person nach Artikel 26 ZG; b. Barmittel: 1. Bargeld (schweizerische und ausländische Banknoten und Münzen, die als Zahlungsmittel im Umlauf sind), 2. übertragbare Inhaberpapiere, Aktien, Obligationen, Schecks und ähnliche Wertpapiere.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 2 Begriffsbestimmungen
pinpoint.locator_note: SR 631.052 legal definition of Barmittel; broader 'ähnliche Wertpapiere' limb vs FOCBS public shorthand (shares, bonds and cheques) | English working gloss (not authority text): For the purposes of this Ordinance: a. person required to provide information: person required to declare under Article 26 of the Customs Act (ZG); b. cash means: 1. cash money (Swiss and foreign banknotes and coins that are in circulation as means of payment), 2. transferable bearer instruments, shares, bonds, cheques and similar securities.

excerpts.source_text: Die auskunftspflichtige Person muss im grenzüberschreitenden Verkehr auf ausdrückliche Befragung hin der Zollstelle Auskunft erteilen: a. zu ihrer Person; b. über die Ein-, Aus- und Durchfuhr von Barmitteln im Betrag von mindestens 10 000 Franken oder entsprechendem Gegenwert bei ausländischen Währungen; c. über die Herkunft und den vorgesehenen Verwendungszweck der Barmittel; d. über die wirtschaftlich berechtigte Person.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 3 Auskunftserteilung
pinpoint.locator_note: Statutory information-on-request package; operator mindestens 10 000 Franken (>= CHF 10,000); covers Ein-/Aus-/Durchfuhr | English working gloss (not authority text): In cross-border traffic, the person required to provide information must, upon express questioning by the customs office, provide information: a. as to their person; b. concerning the import, export and transit of cash amounting to at least CHF 10,000 or the corresponding equivalent in foreign currencies; c. concerning the origin and the intended use of the cash; d. concerning the beneficial owner.

excerpts.source_text: Bei Verdacht auf Geldwäscherei oder Terrorismusfinanzierung kann die Zollstelle auch Auskünfte verlangen, wenn der Betrag der Barmittel den Schwellenwert von 10 000 Franken oder den entsprechenden Gegenwert bei ausländischen Währungen nicht erreicht.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 3 Auskunftserteilung
pinpoint.locator_note: Below-threshold suspicion information limb; separate from the >= CHF 10,000 Art. 3 Abs. 1 package | English working gloss (not authority text): Where there is suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing, the customs office may also require information if the amount of cash does not reach the threshold of CHF 10,000 or the corresponding equivalent in foreign currencies.

excerpts.source_text: Die Zollstelle kann nach Artikel 104 ZG Barmittel vorläufig beschlagnahmen. Die vorläufige Beschlagnahme ist unabhängig vom Betrag der Barmittel zulässig.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 4 Vorläufige Beschlagnahme
pinpoint.locator_note: Provisional seizure power under Art. 104 ZG; amount-independent; not automatic confiscation at CHF 10,000 | English working gloss (not authority text): The customs office may provisionally seize cash pursuant to Article 104 of the Customs Act (ZG). Provisional seizure is permissible independent of the amount of cash.

excerpts.source_text: Die verweigerte oder falsche Erteilung einer Auskunft nach Artikel 3 Absatz 1 Buchstaben a und b gilt als Ordnungswidrigkeit im Sinne von Artikel 127 Absatz 1 ZG.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 5 Strafbestimmung
pinpoint.locator_note: Statutory offence characterisation for refused/false information on identity and import/export/transit of >=CHF10k cash limbs (Art. 3 Abs. 1 lit. a–b) | English working gloss (not authority text): Refused or false provision of information under Article 3 paragraph 1 letters a and b constitutes an administrative offence within the meaning of Article 127 paragraph 1 of the Customs Act (ZG).

excerpts.source_text: Die Meldung ist unabhängig vom Betrag der Barmittel zulässig.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 6 Meldung der Zollstellen
pinpoint.locator_note: Amount-independent statutory reporting permission to Oberzolldirektion; keep distinct from FOCBS public >=CHF10k information-system entry narrative | English working gloss (not authority text): The report is permissible independent of the amount of cash.

excerpts.source_text: When establishing a business relationship, the financial intermediary must verify the identity of the customer on the basis of a document of evidentiary value. Where the customer is a legal entity, the financial intermediary must acknowledge the provisions regulating the power to bind the legal entity, and verify the identity of the persons who enter into the business relationship on behalf of the legal entity.

pinpoint.heading: Verification of the identity of the customer
pinpoint.locator_note: AMLA Art. 3 para. 1 contracting-party/customer identity at business-relationship establishment

excerpts.notes: Hardening II accounts/AML evidence. Does not establish statutory account entitlement.

excerpts.source_text: The financial intermediary must identify the beneficial owner with the due diligence required in the circumstances and verify its identity in order to ensure that it knows who the beneficial owner is. If the customer is a listed company or a subsidiary over which a listed company has majority control, the identity of the beneficial owner need not be established.

pinpoint.heading: Establishing the identity of the beneficial owner
pinpoint.locator_note: AMLA Art. 4 para. 1 beneficial-owner identify+verify (post-1 Jan 2023 wording); listed-company exception retained

excerpts.notes: Hardening II accounts/AML evidence. Does not establish statutory account entitlement.

excerpts.source_text: If doubt arises in the course of the business relationship as to the identity of the customer or of the beneficial owner, the verification of identity or establishment of identity in terms of Articles 3 and 4 respectively must be repeated.

pinpoint.heading: Repetition of the verification of the identity of the customer or the establishment of the identity of the beneficial owner
pinpoint.locator_note: AMLA Art. 5 para. 1 event-driven repetition on doubt — not continuous re-verification of every customer

excerpts.notes: Hardening II accounts/AML evidence. Does not establish statutory account entitlement.

excerpts.source_text: The financial intermediary must clarify the economic background and the purpose of a transaction or of a business relationship if: a. the transaction or the business relationship appears unusual, unless its legality is clear; b. there are indications that assets are the proceeds of a felony or an aggravated tax misdemeanour under Article 305 bis number 1 bis SCC or are subject to the power of disposal of a criminal or terrorist organisation (Art. 260 ter SCC) or serve the financing of terrorism (Art. 260 quinquies para. 1 SCC); c. the transaction or the business relationship carries a higher risk; d. the data on a customer, a beneficial owner or an authorised signatory in a business relationship or transaction are identical or very similar to the data passed on to the financial intermediary under Article 22 a paragraph 2 or 3.

excerpts.source_text: Pecuniary debts must be discharged in legal tender of the currency in which the debt was incurred.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 84
pinpoint.locator_note: CO Art. 84 para. 1 — pecuniary debts payable in legal tender of the currency owed

excerpts.notes: H3. Monetary-obligation currency of discharge. Not an invoicing, bank-execution, or transfer-freedom rule.

excerpts.source_text: A debt expressed in a currency other than the national currency of the place of payment may be discharged in that national currency at the rate of exchange that applies on the day it falls due, unless literal performance is required by inclusion in the contract of the expression ‘actual currency’ or words to that effect.

pinpoint.heading: Art. 84
pinpoint.locator_note: CO Art. 84 para. 2 — local-currency substitution at maturity exchange rate; 'actual currency' exception

excerpts.notes: H3. Captures both substitution limb and literal-performance exception in one official paragraph; separate candidates keep the limbs atomic. Official EN 'actual currency' = DE 'effektiv'.

excerpts.source_text: For purposes of calculating the VAT payable, considerations paid in foreign currency must be converted into national currency at the date the tax claim arises.

pinpoint.section: Chapter 3 Assessment Basis and Tax Rates / Section 1 Assessment Basis
pinpoint.heading: Considerations in foreign currency
pinpoint.locator_note: VAT Ordinance Art. 45 para. 1 — FCY considerations converted to CHF for VAT calculation

excerpts.notes: H3. Tax calculation conversion. ≠ contractual settlement must be in CHF.

excerpts.source_text: A consideration is in foreign currency if the invoice or the receipt is issued in foreign currency. If no invoice or receipt is issued, the book entry of the supplier applies. It is irrelevant whether the payment is in national or foreign currency and in which currency the change is paid.

pinpoint.section: Chapter 3 Assessment Basis and Tax Rates / Section 1 Assessment Basis
pinpoint.heading: Considerations in foreign currency
pinpoint.locator_note: VAT Ordinance Art. 45 para. 2 — FCY invoice defines FCY consideration; payment currency distinct

excerpts.notes: H3. Shows VAT treats foreign-currency invoices as FCY considerations and separates invoice currency from payment currency. Does not alone create a universal private-law right to invoice in any currency.

excerpts.source_text: Considerations in foreign currency need to be converted into Swiss francs for the purposes of calculating the domestic tax and the reverse charge at the time the tax claim arises. The calculation of the recoverable input tax is based on the consideration at the time the input tax is deductible. For the conversion, either the monthly average rate published by the Federal Tax Administration FTA or the daily exchange rate (sell) can be used.

pinpoint.heading: Foreign currency exchange rates VAT
pinpoint.locator_note: FTA VAT FX guidance — convert FCY considerations to CHF for VAT using FTA monthly average or daily sell rate

excerpts.notes: H3. FTA corroboration of VAT FX conversion mechanics. Tax reporting ≠ payment prohibition.

excerpts.source_text: Accounting is carried out in the national currency or in the currency required for business operations.

excerpts.notes: H3. Accounting currency ≠ invoice currency ≠ payment currency ≠ bank-account currency.

excerpts.source_text: Financial reports are presented in the national currency or in the currency required for business operations. If the national currency is not used, the values must also be shown in the national currency. The exchange rates applied must be published in the notes to the accounts and if applicable explained.

excerpts.source_text: The Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) payment system is Switzerland's central payment system. Since its launch on 10 June 1987, it has been operated by SIX Interbank Clearing Ltd (SIC Ltd) on behalf of the Swiss National Bank. The participants eligible to use SIC primarily include Swiss banks and other financial market participants. As well as large-value transactions, the SIC system also processes retail payments connected with services provided by financial market participants (bank transfers, card payments, direct debits, etc.).

pinpoint.heading: The Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) payment system
pinpoint.locator_note: SNB SIC page — central CHF payment system; large-value and retail rails for participants

excerpts.notes: H3. Infrastructure mechanics. Not universal entitlement; not SNB per-payment approval.

excerpts.source_text: Instant payments allow private individuals and companies to settle domestic account-to-account transactions with immediate execution and final settlement in seconds - 24 hours a day, 7 days a week (including public holidays).

pinpoint.heading: SNB and ECB explore interlinking of instant payment systems
pinpoint.locator_note: SNB 29 Sep 2025 press — domestic instant payments definition

excerpts.notes: H3. Domestic instant-payment mechanics only.

excerpts.source_text: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the European Central Bank (ECB) are launching an exploration phase to evaluate an interlinking between the instant payment service (IP service) of the SIC system, and TIPS, the Eurosystem's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement service. The aim is to assess the feasibility and economic viability of such an interlinking. This exploration phase will continue throughout 2026.

pinpoint.heading: SNB and ECB explore interlinking of instant payment systems
pinpoint.locator_note: SNB 29 Sep 2025 — SIC IP / TIPS interlinking exploration throughout 2026

excerpts.notes: H3. Temporal/exploratory. Not current cross-currency instant production rail.

excerpts.source_text: On 19 December 2025, Parliament adopted the Investment Screening Act (ISA). It aims to safeguard public order and security by subjecting acquisitions of Swiss companies operating in especially critical sectors by foreign state-controlled investors to prior approval. Entry into force is expected in 2027.

excerpts.source_text: Die Finanzintermediäre werden gemäss den Vorschriften der Verordnung aufgefordert, die Verbote umzusetzen, die Vermögenswerte der sanktionierten Personen zu sperren und dem SECO die betroffenen Geschäftsbeziehungen zu melden. Die Meldung an das SECO entbindet einen Finanzintermediär nicht davon, bei Verdachtsmomenten zusätzliche Abklärungen gemäss Art. 6 GwG vorzunehmen und falls er diese nicht ausräumen kann, unverzüglich bei der Meldestelle für Geldwäscherei gemäss Art. 9 GwG eine Meldung zu erstatten.
